newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes executives angry at Schrempp - report.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes executives angry at Schrempp - report.

text.p: Executives at Mercedes-Benz AG have complained with the company's top brass that discussions about restructuring its parent, the Daimler-Benz group, were unsettling the workforce, weekly Der Spiegel said on Saturday.

A committee of executives at the German luxury car maker has written a letter expressing consternation over the lack of candor in discussions about restructuring Daimler, Der Spiegel said in a report made available ahead of publication on Monday.

The letter states that public statements about the internal discussions "have given leading managers deep sense of insecurity concerning the future direction of our company" and urged top management to decide on the restructuring quickly.

A Daimler spokesman said dicussions about the company's future structure were being conducted in a calmer atmosphere now and that the committee of leading executives was constantly kept abreast of new developments.

Daimler chairman Juergen Schrempp is believed to favour merging the car maker with the Daimler group and bringing Mercedes chairman Helmut Werner and three other Mercedes executives onto Daimler's management board.
Werner prefers to keep Mercedes as an independent division and has opposed the plan.
Daimler's supervisory board is expected to decide on the restructuring plan at an extraordinary meeting on January 23.
